<issue identifier="MM-411">
<title>Re-key migration: move existing (old-model) accounts onto client-generated shares + recovery rotation key</title>
<description>
Phase 2–3 bridge of <issue id="5ec229fb-5497-4ace-8295-ad2b83985a7a" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-405/key-recovery-from-shares-bind-the-escrowed-secret-and-build-the">MM-405</issue>. Design: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-key-recovery-from-shares.md` §7.

Every pre-existing account carries the old model: a server-generated split of an unbound secret. Those shares protect nothing (the honest framing — they are *voided*, not rotated), and the material was server-visible at generation. Until re-key, such an account's only safety net is the device key itself.

## Scoping (production-migration review, 2026-07-17)

* **did:plc only.** A did:web identity has no PLC `rotationKeys` — its control model is domain/hosting control, so the recovery-rotation-key concept doesn't map. The detection must skip did:web identities entirely (no prompt, no error); share-based recovery for did:web is a separate design question, noted in the design doc's open questions.
* **Wallet-native identities only.** Interop accounts migrated in via standard `createAccount` never entered the Shamir model (no `/v1/dids` ceremony, no shares) and manage their own rotation keys — nothing to re-key. They adopt the new model only if/when they adopt the wallet.
* **Lazy by construction.** Only the device key can sign the re-key op, so there is no server-driven bulk migration and no deadline pressure: an un-re-keyed account is exactly as protected as it is today (device key only). The prompt appears on next wallet open, per DID.
* **Additive-only safety property.** The device key stays at `rotationKeys[0]` through every step; shares are generated and locally persisted *before* the PLC op; escrow deposit follows it. A failure at any step leaves the account no less recoverable than the status quo, and resume converges to the same terminal state. There is no window in which the account is worse off.

## Scope

**Wallet:**

* Detect the old model per identity: **did:plc** + authoritative [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) doc has no recovery key at `rotationKeys[1]` (2-key array = old model).
* Prompt (calm, non-alarmist — this is an upgrade, not an incident) and run the re-key: generate seed + split client-side (envelope v2) → device-key-signed PLC rotation op inserting the recovery key at `[1]` (device stays `[0]`, PDS key shifts to `[2]`) → `PUT /v1/recovery/escrow-share` → rewrite Keychain `recovery-share-1` → walk the user through saving the new Share 3 (reuse `ShamirBackupScreen`).
* After the op lands, trigger `refreshIdentity` so the PDS-side cached doc heals (the <issue id="d87c4698-7a8e-4373-92bb-64dffb8ec5d8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-300/post-migrationrecovery-did-doc-cache-stores-the-w3c-document-home">MM-300</issue> class of staleness).
* Resumable at every step (PLC op landed but escrow not deposited, etc. — persist progress like the migration orchestrator does).
* Multi-identity wallets: per-DID, not per-app.

**PDS:**

* On successful escrow deposit for a DID with a legacy `accounts.recovery_share`, null the legacy column (it's dead material).
* Once fleet adoption allows, a follow-up migration drops `accounts.recovery_share` entirely (tracked here; can ship later).

## Acceptance

* Old-model did:plc identity in the harness: full re-key ends with 3 rotation keys on the doc, envelope-v2 escrow row, legacy column NULL, old Keychain share overwritten.
* A did:web identity and a new-model identity never see the prompt.
* Interrupt-and-resume at each step lands in the same terminal state; at no intermediate state is recovery capability below the pre-re-key baseline.
* `plc_monitor` treats the wallet's own re-key op as authorized (signed by the device key — should already hold, but assert it: the re-key must not trigger a tamper alert).
</description>

<title>Key recovery from shares — bind the escrowed secret and build the recovery ceremony (epic)</title>
<description>
Umbrella for the design captured in `docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-key-recovery-from-shares.md` (branch `claude/key-recovery-shares-l0n8zm`).

## The gap

The as-built 2-of-3 Shamir split recovers **nothing**: the secret is a fresh random 32 bytes generated *server-side* in `create_did.rs`, bound to no rotation key and encrypting nothing. The Secure-Enclave device key was never splittable (non-extractable), so recovery must ride a separate software key — which doesn't exist. Compounding it: the escrow agent (Custos) saw the secret and all three shares at ceremony time, and `pending_accounts.pending_share_{1,2,3}` puts full reconstruction material into Litestream backups. ADR-0001, the docs site (`user/backup.md`), and the V046 admin-repair doctrine all promise a ceremony that doesn't exist. The passwordless plan (<issue id="ff3e493f-009c-4211-b4de-4ed9a2e7d1a4" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-312/passwordless-auth-retire-the-account-password-in-favor-of-device">MM-312</issue>) names this its **hard prerequisite**.

## The design, in one paragraph

The secret becomes a **recovery seed**: HKDF-derive a P-256 keypair from it and place its did:key in `rotationKeys` as `[device, recovery, PDS]` (3 of PLC's 5 key slots; device stays supreme so a share-collecting operator can never outrank the enclave — the 72h override backstop). Generation moves **client-side** (the wallet already links `crates/crypto`), so the server only ever holds Share 2. Reconstruction is verifiable against the public DID doc, and — because `/v1/sessions/sovereign` accepts any current rotation key — a recovered wallet can authenticate passwordlessly before the key-replacement PLC op even lands. Two ceremonies: **escrow-assisted** (Share 1 iCloud + Share 2 released via email OTP behind rate limits/audit/cancellable delay) and **fully sovereign** (Share 1 + Share 3, zero server involvement, composing with ADR-0002 migration for credible exit).

## Child issues (dependency order)

1. Crypto primitives: share envelope v2 + seed-derived recovery keypair + multi-rotation-key genesis builder
2. Ceremony inversion: client-side share generation, recovery key in genesis, single-share escrow (+ ordering ADR)
3. PDS escrow storage: `recovery_escrow` table, KEK wrapping (absorbs <issue id="619eda03-07be-4705-aee4-39e12cdaf0f8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-378/kek-wrap-the-escrow-shamir-share-accountsrecovery-share-at-rest">MM-378</issue>), owner endpoints, audit trail
4. PDS escrow release: initiate/release/cancel with email OTP, delay window, rate limits
5. Wallet recovery ceremony: both paths + re-anchor + share-rotation epilogue
6. Re-key migration for existing (old-model) accounts
7. Docs truth-up (immediately actionable — current docs claim untrue things)
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

2	
3	Status: **accepted for implementation** — tracked in Linear as

18	
19	## Problem
20	
21	Every layer of the stack promises share-based recovery, and none of it can currently
22	recover anything:
23	
24	- ADR-0001 names the mitigation for its "user key loss" failure mode: "2-of-3 Shamir
25	  splitting of the device key at onboarding … Full 2-of-3 recovery ceremony is future
26	  work."
27	- The docs site tells users "Obsign brings any two shares back together and reconstructs
28	  the recovery key on your device" ([user/backup.md](../../sites/docs/src/content/docs/user/backup.md)) —
29	  a flow that does not exist.
30	- The V046 admin-repair doctrine refuses password-reset tokens for passwordless accounts
31	  because "a key-sovereign account is recovered through its escrowed key share."
32	
33	This document audits what actually ships today, names the gaps, and designs the two
34	recovery paths the split was always meant to enable:
35	
36	- **With escrow assistance** — lost phone, iCloud intact: Share 1 (iCloud) + Share 2
37	  (Custos escrow) recover on a new device, with the server as a *release gate*.
38	- **Without escrow assistance** — Custos dead, hostile, or simply not trusted: Share 1 +
39	  Share 3 (user's copy) recover with **zero** server involvement, composing with
40	  ADR-0002's wallet-authorized migration for full credible exit.
41	
42	## Current state (as-built audit)
43	
44	**The crypto layer is solid.** `crates/crypto/src/shamir.rs` implements a hardened 2-of-3
45	split of a 32-byte secret over GF(2^8) (branchless reduction on secret bytes, zeroized
46	share material, information-theoretic single-share security). `split_secret` /
47	`combine_shares` are tested and ready.
48	
49	**The distribution plumbing works as designed.** The `/v1/dids` ceremony
50	(`crates/pds/src/routes/create_did.rs`) generates shares, returns Shares 1 and 3 to the
51	wallet, and commits Share 2 to `accounts.recovery_share` (V010) atomically with
52	promotion. Retries are idempotent via `pending_accounts.pending_share_{1,2,3}` (V011).
53	The wallet stores Share 1 in the iCloud-synced Keychain (`recovery-share-1`) and walks
54	the user through saving Share 3 (`ShamirBackupScreen`, confirm-before-continue).
55	
56	**But the model has five gaps, in severity order:**
57	
58	1. **The secret is bound to nothing.** `generate_recovery_shares()` splits a *fresh
59	   random 32 bytes*. That secret is not a rotation key, does not appear in the DID's
60	   `rotationKeys`, and encrypts nothing. Reconstructing it recovers a random number.
61	   The device key it was nominally protecting lives in the Secure Enclave and is
62	   non-extractable — it never could have been the split's input on real hardware.
63	
64	2. **The escrow agent generated the secret.** The split runs *server-side*: the PDS saw
65	   the secret and all three shares at ceremony time, and `pending_accounts` holds all
66	   three in plaintext until promotion — which means Litestream backups and WAL history
67	   retain complete reconstruction material for every account that ran the ceremony.
68	   Today's impact is nil only because of gap 1: the moment the secret is bound to real
69	   authority, server-side generation breaks the sovereignty claim ("the PDS holds at
70	   most one share" — [data-migration-spec](../data-migration-spec.md)) for every
71	   existing account, retroactively and unfixably for anyone holding old backups.
72	
73	3. **The specs describe an impossible reconstruction.** The
74	   [mobile spec §7](../mobile-architecture-spec.md) says recovery "reconstruct[s the]
75	   root key in new Secure Enclave" — SE keys cannot be imported. And
76	   [identity-and-key-custody.md](../architecture/identity-and-key-custody.md) says "the
77	   crypto crate splits the device key 2-of-3" — wrong on both counts (not the device
78	   key; not split client-side). The correct model (below): the reconstructed seed
79	   derives a *separate software rotation key*; the new device's SE key is fresh and gets
80	   *installed* by a PLC op that the recovery key signs.
81	
82	4. **Bare share format.** Shares are 52 base32 chars of raw payload: no version, no
83	   share-set id, no index, no checksum. The index isn't even encoded — holders must
84	   remember which share they are by storage location. Two shares from different
85	   generations (e.g. after a future rotation) would combine into silent garbage.
86	
87	5. **Escrow storage is outside the KEK envelope.** `accounts.recovery_share` is
88	   plaintext TEXT — not in `db/kek.rs`'s `SecretFamily::ALL`, so master-key rotation
89	   doesn't cover it. A lone share is information-theoretically useless, so this is
90	   defense-in-depth rather than a break, but it's an inconsistency with every other
91	   secret column.
92	
93	## Design
94	
95	### 1. Bind the seed to real authority: a derived recovery rotation key
96	
97	The 32-byte secret becomes a **recovery seed**. From it, derive a P-256 keypair
98	(HKDF-SHA256 with a fixed domain-separation info string → scalar, rejection-sampled into
99	the curve order), and place its `did:key` in the DID's `rotationKeys`:
100	
101	> The derivation must be canonical so an independent implementation reconstructs the
102	> identical key from the same seed. The exact byte layout — HKDF salt/IKM/`info`,
103	> candidate scalar length and endianness, the retry-counter encoding and update rule for
104	> rejection sampling, and the `1 ≤ k < n` acceptance range (P-256 order `n`) — is pinned
105	> as golden test vectors in MM-406 (`derive_recovery_keypair`), not hand-specified here;
106	> this doc fixes the *construction*, MM-406 fixes the *bytes*.
107	
108	```text
109	rotationKeys: [ device key (SE),  recovery key (derived),  PDS key ]
110	                    [0]                  [1]                 [2]
111	```
112	
113	The PDS's own signing key keeps its existing dual role — it moves from `rotationKeys[1]`
114	to `[2]`, but stays bound to `verificationMethods.atproto` and remains the repo-commit
115	signer. Only its rotation-priority position changes; the recovery key is inserted above
116	it, never in place of it. (The genesis builder work in MM-406 carries a round-trip test
117	over the `[device, recovery, PDS]` ordering to pin exactly this.)
118	
119	Now reconstruction ⇒ a private key that plc.directory already recognizes as an identity
120	controller. Two properties fall out for free:
121	
122	- **Verifiable reconstruction.** Derive the public key from the combined seed and compare
123	  against the DID's authoritative `rotationKeys` — the wallet can tell the user "these
124	  two shares are correct" (or not) using only public information, before signing anything.
125	- **Passwordless session bootstrap.** `POST /v1/sessions/sovereign` accepts a proof
126	  signed by *any* current PLC rotation key. A recovered wallet can authenticate to
127	  Custos with the recovery key immediately after reconstruction — before the
128	  key-replacement PLC op even lands. The recovery ceremony and the passwordless design
129	  compose instead of colliding.
130	
131	**Why recovery sits below the device key.** Priority only matters inside plc.directory's
132	72-hour override contest. Ordering `[device, recovery, PDS]` means: a *lost* device is
133	recoverable (no contest — the recovery key can freely sign the op replacing it); a
134	*compromised share pair* (iCloud + escrow, i.e. a malicious operator colluding with an
135	Apple-account compromise) can still be overridden by the genuine device within 72 hours
136	— the Secure Enclave stays supreme, which is the ADR-0001 posture. The alternative
137	(`[recovery, device, PDS]`) would protect against a stolen-and-unlocked device at the
138	cost of letting a share-collecting operator outrank the user's enclave; that inverts the
139	project's core custody claim. (An attacker who can sign with the SE key already owns the
140	unlocked device + biometrics — a stronger position than any share pair, and one no
141	ordering fixes.) Held as an open question below, but the recommendation is firm.
142	
143	### 2. Move generation client-side
144	
145	The wallet's Rust core already links `crates/crypto`. The ceremony changes:
146	
147	- The **wallet** generates the seed, derives the recovery key, splits the seed 2-of-3,
148	  and includes the recovery `did:key` in the genesis op's `rotationKeys` (it already
149	  builds and signs the genesis op via `build_did_plc_genesis_op_with_external_signer`).
150	- `/v1/dids` **stops generating and returning shares** (`shamir_share_1/3` leave the
151	  response; `pending_share_{1,2,3}` and the server-side `generate_recovery_shares` are
152	  retired). The server receives exactly one share — Share 2 — in the ceremony request
153	  (or an immediately-following authenticated `PUT`), and never sees the seed or the
154	  other shares.
155	- Retry-resilience moves where the material now lives: the wallet persists the seed +
156	  all shares in a **non-synced** Keychain staging slot until the ceremony is confirmed
157	  complete. The teardown order is load-bearing — Share 1 must reach its **iCloud-synced**
158	  Keychain slot (`recovery-share-1`) and that write must be verified, and Share 3
159	  confirmation must be complete, *before* the seed and Share 2's local copy are zeroized.
160	  The staging slot (non-synced, transient) and the Share 1 slot (synced, durable) are
161	  deliberately different homes; losing the seed before Share 1 is durably synced would
162	  strand recovery.
163	
164	This closes gap 2 structurally: reconstruction material never exists server-side, so no
165	DB snapshot, backup, or hostile operator can ever hold two shares.
166	
167	### 3. Versioned share envelope
168	
169	Replace bare base32 with a self-describing envelope (still base32/QR-friendly):
170	
171	```text
172	version(1B) || set_id(4B) || index(1B) || payload(32B) || checksum(4B, SHA-256 prefix over the preceding bytes)
173	```
174	
175	- `set_id`: random per split-generation; `combine` refuses shares from different sets
176	  loudly instead of reconstructing garbage (fixes gap 4, prerequisite for rotation).
177	- `index`: carried in-band; holders no longer identify shares by storage location.
178	- Share 3 additionally gets a **BIP-39-style word rendering** for the human-custody copy
179	  (the mobile spec always envisioned this); Shares 1/2 stay machine-format.
180	- `crates/crypto` gains `encode_share`/`decode_share` plus the HKDF
181	  `derive_recovery_keypair(seed)`; the GF(2^8) core is unchanged.
182	
183	### 4. Recovery ceremony A — with escrow assistance
184	
185	The common case: lost/dead phone, iCloud intact, Custos alive and honest.
186	
187	1. **New device, fresh install** → "Recover existing identity." Share 1 appears
188	   automatically via iCloud Keychain sync.
189	2. **Escrow release request.** `POST /v1/recovery/initiate` with handle/DID → server
190	   emails an OTP to the account address (always-200, no enumeration — the
191	   `requestPasswordReset` pattern; real delivery exists since MM-211).
192	   `POST /v1/recovery/release` with the OTP **opens a release** (it does not
193	   immediately hand back the share when the delay is on — see step 3). Every step: tight
194	   per-IP rate limits, audit events, and a notification to the account email.
195	3. **Release delay (default on, operator- and user-configurable).** The release enters a
196	   `pending` state for a window (e.g. 24h) during which any authenticated session/device
197	   can cancel — a push through the [notification relay](2026-07-10-notification-relay.md)
198	   when that lands, email links meanwhile. The state machine (detailed in MM-409) is:
199	   the OTP is single-use and consumed by the opening `release` call, which returns
200	   `{status: "pending", available_at}`; the client then **re-polls the same
201	   `release` endpoint** (now authenticated by the opened release's own handle, not the
202	   spent OTP), which returns `pending` until `available_at`, then the Share 2 envelope
203	   once — with a zero-length delay collapsing this to a single call that returns the
204	   share directly. Rationale: escrow release converts "iCloud + mailbox compromise" into
205	   identity compromise; the delay plus the device key's 72-hour override supremacy
206	   (ordering above) are the two backstops. A requester who can't wait can skip the delay
207	   by proving possession of Share 3 — at which point they hold two shares and never
208	   needed escrow.
209	4. **Reconstruct + verify.** Combine Shares 1+2 → seed → derive keypair → compare the
210	   public key against plc.directory's current `rotationKeys`. Mismatch = wrong/stale
211	   shares, fail loudly before any signature.
212	5. **Re-anchor the identity.** The new device generates a fresh SE device key; the
213	   recovery key signs a PLC rotation op replacing the old device key at
214	   `rotationKeys[0]` with the new one. Sovereign session via the recovery key
215	   bootstraps Custos auth for the new device's session/device registration.
216	6. **Rotate the shares.** Mandatory ceremony epilogue: new seed, new split, new
217	   recovery key replacing the old at `rotationKeys[1]` (same or follow-up op, signed by
218	   the new device key), new Share 2 re-escrowed over the authenticated session, Share 1
219	   rewritten to Keychain, user walked through saving the new Share 3. The lost device's
220	   world — old Share 1 copy, old escrow, old Share 3 — is fully void.
221	
222	### 5. Recovery ceremony B — without escrow assistance
223	
224	The credible-exit case: Custos is down, hostile, or the user simply doesn't want to ask.
225	
226	1. Share 1 (iCloud Keychain) + Share 3 (manual entry / QR / word-phrase) combine
227	   **entirely on-device**. No Custos endpoint is touched.
228	2. Verify against plc.directory as above (the only network dependency).
229	3. The recovery key signs PLC op(s) that: install the new device key, and — when the
230	   old PDS is gone — repoint `services.atproto_pds` and swap
231	   `verificationMethods.atproto` to a new host's keys. This is exactly ADR-0002's
232	   wallet-authorized migration with the recovery key standing in for the lost device
233	   key. Repo data restoration then follows the standard import path
234	   (`getRepo` from relay/AppView mirrors, `importRepo` at the new host).
235	4. Share rotation epilogue as in ceremony A (escrow upload goes to whichever PDS the
236	   identity now points at).
237	
238	**What escrow alone can never do — by design.** Custos holds one share and the
239	lowest-priority rotation key. A pure-escrow "recovery" is impossible (one share reveals
240	nothing), and the PDS's own `rotationKeys[2]` remains only the interop-grade,
241	email-tokened `signPlcOperation` lever it is today — overridable by both keys above it.
242	Both properties should be stated in the docs as guarantees, not caveats.
243	
244	### 6. Server surface (sketch)
245	
246	| Endpoint | Auth | Purpose |
247	|---|---|---|
248	| `PUT /v1/recovery/escrow-share` | account owner (session / sovereign session) | store or replace Share 2; used at ceremony, rotation, and old-model migration |
249	| `POST /v1/recovery/initiate` | public, rate-limited | handle/DID → email OTP; always-200 |
250	| `POST /v1/recovery/release` | OTP | enter `pending` (delayed) or return Share 2; audit + notify |
251	| `POST /v1/recovery/release/cancel` | any account session/device | kill a pending release |
252	| `DELETE /v1/recovery/escrow-share` | account owner | opt out of escrow entirely (Shares 1+3 remain the only path) |
253	
254	Storage moves from the `accounts.recovery_share` column to a `recovery_escrow` table
255	(share envelope ciphertext, created/rotated timestamps, release state machine) plus an
256	append-only `recovery_audit_events` (modeled on `agent_audit_events`). The escrowed
257	share is AES-256-GCM-wrapped under the master KEK and **registered in
258	`SecretFamily::ALL`** so `rewrap-master-key` covers it (fixes gap 5).
259	`account_delete::purge_account` deletes both tables' rows.
260	
261	The wrapping reuses the crate's existing `crypto::encrypt_private_key` envelope —
262	`base64(nonce(12) ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag(16))` with a **fresh random nonce per call**
263	(documented in `crates/crypto/AGENTS.md`), the same envelope every other `SecretFamily`
264	column already uses — so nonce-uniqueness and tag storage come for free and
265	`rewrap-master-key` discovers and rewrites the column exactly as it does the others (it
266	decrypts every `SecretFamily::ALL` ciphertext under the old master key and re-encrypts
267	under the new one in a single stopped-server transaction, never logging plaintext; a KEK
268	version isn't stored per-row because the whole DB is at one `kek_generation`). Whether to
269	additionally bind `(did, set_id, version)` as AES-GCM **AAD** — cheap tamper-evidence
270	that an escrow row can't be transplanted between accounts — is an MM-408 implementation
271	choice; the base envelope does not today, and adopting it for this column would be a
272	deliberate divergence from the shared `encrypt_private_key` helper worth its own note.
273	
274	### 7. Migrating existing accounts
275	
276	Every pre-existing account has an unbound, server-generated split — worthless as-is and
277	tainted per gap 2. The wallet detects the old model (no recovery key in `rotationKeys`)
278	and runs a **re-key**: generate seed client-side, device-key-signed PLC op inserts the
279	recovery key at `[1]`, `PUT` the new Share 2 (server drops `accounts.recovery_share`),
280	rewrite Keychain Share 1, walk the user through saving the new Share 3 (reusing
281	`ShamirBackupScreen`). Until re-key, the account's real safety net is unchanged from
282	today: the device key itself. Old shares are voided by the re-key, not merely rotated —
283	which is the honest framing, since they never protected anything.
284	
285	## Implementation seams (verified 2026-07-17)
286	
287	A pre-scheduling pass over the actual code confirmed the design lands on friendly seams:
288	
289	- **The genesis builder is the only hard-coded constraint.**
290	  `build_did_plc_genesis_op[_with_external_signer]` fixes
291	  `rotation_keys: vec![rotation_key, signing_key]`; a multi-key variant is needed
292	  (MM-406). The server's `verify_and_validate_genesis_op` only pins `rotationKeys[0]`
293	  and non-emptiness — a third key already passes validation unchanged.
294	- **PLC's cap is 1–5 rotation *keys*** (not rotation operations). The proposed layout
295	  spends 3 of 5 slots, deliberately leaving headroom for a second device or
296	  successor-key arrangement; k-of-n growth stays inside the one recovery key.
297	- **Sovereign session needs zero changes** for the recovery-key bootstrap:
298	  `/v1/sessions/sovereign` already verifies against the authoritative current PLC
299	  `rotationKeys`, any key qualifying.
300	- **Established patterns cover the new server surface:** the OTP reuses the hashed
301	  single-use 1-hour token envelope (V014/V033/V034/V036); the release pair shares one
302	  per-endpoint IP limiter instance (the agent claim-pair precedent); the audit trail
303	  copies `agent_audit_events` (V040, append-only); the escrow ciphertext registers as a
304	  new `SecretFamily` variant so `rewrap-master-key` covers it (absorbing MM-378).
305	
306	## Suggested phasing (when scheduled)
307	
308	1. **Crypto + format** (`crates/crypto`): share envelope v2 (encode/decode, set-id
309	   check), `derive_recovery_keypair`. Pure, fully testable offline.
310	2. **Ceremony inversion**: wallet-side generation/split, recovery key in genesis
311	   `rotationKeys`, `PUT /v1/recovery/escrow-share`, retire server-side generation +
312	   `pending_share_*`, escrow table + KEK wrapping, re-key flow for existing accounts.
313	   Spec/docs corrections (identity-and-key-custody.md, mobile spec §7, user backup.md).
314	3. **Recovery ceremonies**: wallet "Recover existing identity" onboarding branch
315	   (both A and B paths share reconstruction/verification/re-anchor code), escrow
316	   release endpoints with OTP + audit + notification, share-rotation epilogue.
317	4. **Hardening**: release-delay state machine with cancel (push via the notification
318	   relay once it lands), periodic "verify your Share 3" health-check prompts, docs-site
319	   recovery runbook.
320	
321	Phases 1–2 are the passwordless plan's hard prerequisite in buildable form; the
322	passwordless Phase 1 should not ship before them.
323	
324	## Open questions
325	
326	- **Rotation-key ordering.** Recommendation above is `[device, recovery, PDS]`
327	  (enclave supremacy). The alternative `[recovery, device, PDS]` favors the
328	  stolen-unlocked-device threat over the malicious-operator threat — worth one explicit
329	  ADR when this is scheduled, since it's near-impossible to change ergonomically later.
330	- **Release-delay default.** 24h? 0 for accounts with a confirmed second device? The
331	  delay's value depends on the notification relay existing; before push, cancel is
332	  email-only and the delay protects less.
333	- **Escrow release identity-proofing for email-less or unconfirmed-email accounts.**
334	  Mobile onboarding collects email, but nothing forces confirmation. Options: require
335	  confirmed email for escrow enrollment; fall back to operator-mediated release via the
336	  admin companion (signed-request audited).
337	- **k-of-n generalization.** The GF(2^8) core generalizes trivially, but 2-of-3 is
338	  hardcoded in `split_secret`'s signature and every holder story. Social-recovery-style
339	  n>3 (friends as holders) is attractive later; the share envelope's `set_id`/`index`
340	  design should not preclude it (1 byte of index allows 255 shares — fine).
341	- **did:web identities.** A did:web account has no PLC `rotationKeys`; its control model
342	  is domain/hosting control, so the recovery-rotation-key design doesn't map. The re-key
343	  migration (MM-411) skips did:web; whether share-based recovery has a did:web analogue
344	  (e.g. an escrowed verification key in the served document) is unexplored. *Production
345	  note (2026-07-17): the operator's did:web identity has not yet migrated onto Custos,
346	  so this is precautionary scoping, not a live migration concern — and a did:web
347	  migration performed after this work lands is unaffected either way.*
348	- ~~**Version-skew transition.**~~ *Resolved 2026-07-17, then **reversed the same day**
349	  by the production-migration review (recorded on MM-407): the earlier resolution
350	  ("single operator-controlled install → hard-cut the legacy path inside MM-407")
351	  underweighted the deploy ordering — Railway deploys the server on `main`/`production`
352	  before the TestFlight wallet build propagates, so a hard cut would break an old wallet
353	  build onboarding a new account mid-ceremony. As built, `/v1/dids` runs **dual-mode**
354	  for a transition window: a request carrying the client-share fields (`recoveryKey` +
355	  `escrowShare`) takes the new path; a legacy-shaped request keeps the old server-side
356	  generation and is flagged in logs for adoption tracking. The legacy path,
357	  `pending_share_{1,2,3}`, and `generate_recovery_shares` retire in a follow-up once the
358	  fleet has updated. (did:web ceremonies stay on the legacy path regardless — see the
359	  did:web open question above.)*
360	- **Seed-derived vs independent recovery key for rotation ops.** Deriving via HKDF makes
361	  reconstruction verifiable against the DID doc with no extra stored state — chosen
362	  here. The cost: the seed *is* the key; share-set rotation is therefore also key
363	  rotation (a PLC op every time). That coupling seems right (rotating shares because
364	  some may be compromised should rotate the key), but worth confirming.

171	        return Err(RotationError::WalletNotAuthorized);

174	    // Rule 2 (freshness).
175	    if inputs.staged_key_id == inputs.device_key_id {
176	        return Err(RotationError::GuardRejected {

Every pre-existing account carries the **old recovery model**: a server-generated 2-of-3 split of a secret bound to nothing — the shares protect nothing and the server saw all three at generation. ## Wallet (`rekey.rs`, new)

Composes the existing MM-407 seams — no new crypto:
- **Detect** old-model per identity: did:plc + authoritative doc has a 2-key `rotationKeys` array (`isOldModelRecovery`). did:web and new-model (3-key) identities are never prompted.
- **Prompt** a calm, seal-toned "Add a recovery key" strip on the home surface (deliberately *not* the critical/alert palette — an upgrade, not an incident).

- **Additive-only + resumable**: the device key never leaves `rotationKeys[0]`, shares are staged before the PLC op, escrow follows it. On a successful escrow deposit, null the dead legacy `accounts.recovery_share` in the **same transaction** and record `legacy_voided` in the escrow audit detail. MM-411 is complete. Here's what shipped and why it holds together.

## Summary

The re-key migration moves pre-existing "old-model" accounts (a server-generated Shamir split of a secret bound to nothing) onto the client-generated recovery model — lazily, per-DID, and additively.

**PDS** — [`recovery_escrow.rs`](crates/pds/src/routes/recovery_escrow.rs): on a successful escrow deposit, the dead legacy `accounts.recovery_share` is nulled in the *same transaction*, with `legacy_voided` recorded in the audit detail.

**Wallet Rust** — [`rekey.rs`](apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/rekey.rs) (new): `build_rekey` → `submit_rekey` → `confirm_rekey`, composing MM-407's seams — client-side seed generation (per-DID staging), a device-key-signed rotation op inserting the recovery key at `rotationKeys[1]`, escrow `PUT` (new `OAuthClient::put`), per-DID Share 1 rewrite, cache refresh.

**Frontend** — a calm seal-toned "Add a recovery key" strip ([`IdentityListHome.svelte`](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/components/home/IdentityListHome.svelte)) and a review→backup→success flow reusing `ShamirBackupScreen`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The safety property is structural, not procedural.** Because the device key never leaves `rotationKeys[0]` and the old shares protected nothing, *every* intermediate state (op-landed-but-escrow-pending, escrow-done-but-Share-1-stale) is exactly as recoverable as the pre-re-key baseline — the device key. That's what lets each step be independently idempotent and the whole thing resume-safe without a durable state machine.
- **Resume detection rides on-chain state + a keychain slot, not a progress enum.** `isOldModelRecovery` (2-key doc) catches un-started re-keys; `rekey_in_progress` (per-DID staging slot) catches ones whose op already landed and now read as new-model — closing the gap where `build_rekey` would otherwise reject with `ALREADY_REKEYED`.
- **`plc_monitor` needed zero code.** Its authorization check is "did *our* device key sign this op?" — signature only, indifferent to what the op does — so a device-signed re-key is authorized for free. I proved it with a test rather than adding logic.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Verification (all four ACs)
- **Live in the browser harness**: drove the full old-model re-key end-to-end (3 rotation keys, new Share 3, staging torn down, strip gone), and confirmed the strip appears *only* on the old-model did:plc identity — never the new-model or did:web ones.
- **Automated**: PDS null-out tests; 13 re-key guard/eligibility tests; per-DID staging tests; the `plc_monitor` authorization test; `isOldModelRecovery` + a full harness integration test (build/submit/confirm, resume idempotence, negative cases). Full wallet suite 455 passed, 41 frontend tests passed, `pnpm check` clean, `clippy -D warnings` clean.

## Notes
- **Deliberate divergence** (documented in design §7 "As built"): re-key uses a **per-DID** `recovery-share-1:{did}` slot rather than the app-global slot the create/migration flows still use — clobbering a sibling's Share 1 would violate the "no state worse off" AC. I filed a follow-up chip to unify create/migration onto per-DID slots (that's a pre-existing multi-identity bug in those flows, out of scope here).
